Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report — a core area of Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Internal Assessment: Fieldwork Report.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Succession means a forest growing taller each year.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.

mcqs.q: Why is GDP per capita a poor measure of wellbeing?
options: GDP measures economic activity, not wellbeing. It ignores inequality, unpaid work, environmental damage and quality of life — high GDP can coexist with poor health, education or happiness.
A high GDP per capita means citizens are happy and well off.
GDP measures the total wealth of every individual in a country.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Succession means a forest growing taller each year.
The sequence of changes in a community of organisms over time, from pioneer species colonising bare ground to a stable climax community matched to local climate.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Succession is just one species replacing another randomly.
